editorial:
Imagine a fancy party where everyone seems happy and open about their marriages, but underneath the surface, everyone is lying. You get thrown right into a group of friends who think they are modern and free, but they are actually just messy. The vibe is tense from the start because you can tell these people don't actually trust each other. When a fatal accident happens during the party, the polite masks fall off, and the real drama begins. You will find yourself wondering who is actually telling the truth and who is just playing a part to look good in front of the others.

What really works here is how the movie handles the secrets. The acting feels real, and the way the tension builds makes you want to know if this was a freak accident or a planned murder. It might feel a bit slow in some spots, but the payoff is worth it. If you enjoy old-school mysteries with a lot of talking and psychology, you should definitely check this out. It is a great pick to rent on Apple TV for a movie night, or you could look for a high-quality 4K Blu-ray to add to your physical collection if you love collecting rare gems.
endingExplained: As the story wraps up, the truth about the accident comes out. You discover that the death wasn't just a random mistake, but the result of deep-seated hatred and jealousy. The twist reveals that the open relationships were a cover for pain and betrayal. In the final scenes, the characters are forced to face their own lies. There is no happy ending, as the guilt and the broken trust leave everyone ruined and alone.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves psychological mysteries and old European cinema.
